rule_text: Under this policy, government-record information is treated as within the publicly-available exemption if it was published no more than 6 months before use, and widely-distributed-media information is treated as within the publicly-available exemption if it was published no more than 18 months before use.
scenario_text: BlueOak Software compiled a marketing list using government-record property ownership filings obtained from a county recorder's office. axis: opt-out preference signal honoring window: financial-incentive-program consumer vs non-participant consumer
rule_text: Under this policy, an opt-out preference signal received from a financial-incentive-program consumer must be honored within 15 days of receipt, and an opt-out preference signal received from a non-participant consumer must be honored within 45 days of receipt.
scenario_text: Northgate Realty detected a browser-based opt-out preference signal from a financial-incentive-program consumer enrolled in its rewards discount plan on August 4. The privacy engineering team flagged the signal in the consent management platform the same day. Northgate Realty applied the opt-out across its advertising vendors 30 days after the signal was detected.

rule_text: An organization experiencing a confirmed-exfiltration incident must notify the relevant regulator within 24 hours of discovery, and an organization experiencing a contained-intrusion incident must notify the relevant regulator within 72 hours of discovery.

Forensic analysis confirmed that approximately 40,000 records left the network before the affected server was isolated. The security team documented the exfiltration timeline and notified internal leadership 48 hours after the compromise was discovered.

axis: ransomware incident reporting timeline: ransom paid vs ransom demanded but not paid
rule_text: Organizations that experience a ransom-payment incident must report the incident to the sector regulator within 48 hours of the event, and organizations that experience a ransom-demand-only incident must report the incident to the sector regulator within 96 hours of the event.

The company's leadership authorized payment of the ransom to obtain a decryption key. The compliance team reported the incident to the sector regulator 72 hours after the encryption was discovered.

axis: de minimis incident reporting exemption: malware contained to a single endpoint vs malware spread across multiple endpoints

axis: third-party risk assessment exemption scope: privileged vendor system access vs reporting-only vendor access

axis: forensic imaging exemption from extended chain-of-custody hold: financial-data system vs marketing-data system
rule_text: Following a suspected compromise, a financial-data-system must be forensically imaged within 12 hours to be exempt from the extended chain-of-custody hold, and a marketing-data-system must be forensically imaged within 36 hours to be exempt from the extended chain-of-custody hold.
scenario_text: Ironvale Credit Union identified suspicious authentication attempts on a server hosting core banking transaction records shortly after a phishing campaign targeted several employees. The incident response team scheduled forensic imaging of the affected server as part of the standard response workflow. Imaging of the financial-data server was completed 24 hours after the suspicious activity was flagged.

rule_text: Data collected under an explicit-consent monitoring authorization may be retained for up to 30 days, and data collected under an implied-consent monitoring authorization may be retained for up to 90 days.
scenario_text: Dunmore Aerospace requires employees to sign an explicit written consent form acknowledging endpoint monitoring before receiving network credentials, and the security team relies on that signed authorization as the basis for its insider-threat detection program. Packet-capture data collected under this program was retained on the SOC's storage array for 60 days following collection.

axis: privileged-session recording review window: court-order-authorized monitoring vs internal-policy-authorized monitoring

axis: keystroke-logging data purge deadline: individualized signed consent vs blanket employment-contract clause
rule_text: Keystroke-logging deployed under individualized-signed-consent authorization must have its collected data purged within 45 days absent an active investigation, and keystroke-logging deployed under blanket-contract-clause authorization must have its collected data purged within 14 days absent an active investigation.
scenario_text: After a contractor at Fennimore Robotics signed an individualized consent form specific to a fraud investigation, the security team deployed keystroke-logging software on the contractor's workstation with that signed authorization as its basis. In the absence of an active investigation, the collected keystroke data remained stored on the monitoring server for 25 days before deletion.

rule_text: A breach affecting a system that processes customer-facing data with more than 250 records exposed requires notification to the data-protection authority, and a breach affecting a system that processes internal-systems-only data with more than 750 records exposed requires notification to the data-protection authority.

axis: data-access request response window: connected-product telemetry data vs related-service usage data
rule_text: A data holder that receives a user request for access to connected-product telemetry data must make that data available without undue delay, and in any event within 15 days of the request, and a data holder that receives a user request for access to related-service usage data must make that data available without undue delay, and in any event within 30 days of the request.
scenario_text: Nordvik Appliances operates a fleet-management portal for its connected refrigeration units and received a formal data-access request from a restaurant chain seeking the telemetry logs generated directly by its units. The company's compliance team logged the request and began compiling the requested telemetry export the same afternoon. The completed data package was delivered to the restaurant chain 22 days after the request was received.

The redacted portion amounted to 17 percent of the full requested dataset.

axis: serious incident reporting timeline: critical-infrastructure high-risk system vs other high-risk system
rule_text: A provider of a high-risk AI system used in critical infrastructure must report a serious incident to the relevant market surveillance authority within 15 days of becoming aware of it, and a provider of a high-risk AI system used in non-critical-infrastructure sectors must report a serious incident to the relevant market surveillance authority within 10 days of becoming aware of it.
scenario_text: Nordholt Grid Systems supplies an AI-based load-balancing tool used to control switching operations across a regional electricity transmission network. On a Tuesday morning, the on-call engineering team detected an anomalous output that briefly de-energized two substations. Nordholt's compliance officer logged the detection and began drafting the incident file the same day. The formal report reached the national market surveillance authority 12 days after the anomaly was first detected.

The internal control assessment file was finalized and signed off 9 months after that start date.

Scenario: Kestrel Diagnostics is preparing to launch an AI system that classifies chest X-ray images to flag suspected fractures for radiologist review, using the internal control conformity route available for its product category. The engineering and quality teams began compiling the technical file and running the required internal tests on 3 January. The internal control assessment file was finalized and signed off 9 months after that start date.

axis: post-market monitoring plan review cadence: high-risk system vs systemic-risk GPAI model
rule_text: A provider of a high-risk AI system must review its post-market monitoring plan at least every 6 months, and a provider of a general-purpose AI model classified as posing systemic risk must review its post-market monitoring plan at least every 12 months.
scenario_text: Aldenberg Mobility markets an AI system that screens loan applications for a network of regional credit unions, classified as high-risk. The compliance team scheduled its post-market monitoring plan reviews around the product's anniversary launch date each cycle. The most recent review was conducted 9 months after the previous one.

axis: technical documentation retention period: GPAI model vs high-risk system
rule_text: A provider of a general-purpose AI model must retain its technical documentation for at least 5 years after the model is withdrawn from the market, and a provider of a high-risk AI system must retain its technical documentation for at least 10 years after the system is withdrawn from the market.
scenario_text: Solvane AI maintained a general-purpose text-generation model that it offered through an API to enterprise customers before discontinuing the offering. After withdrawing the model, Solvane's records team moved the technical documentation into a long-term archive. The archived documentation was scheduled for deletion 7 years after the withdrawal date.

axis: exemption scope: retroactive judicial authorization window for urgent real-time RBI use cases
rule_text: Law enforcement conducting urgent use of real-time remote biometric identification to search for a missing child must obtain retroactive judicial authorization within 24 hours of deployment, and law enforcement conducting urgent use of real-time remote biometric identification to search for a suspect in a minor offense must obtain retroactive judicial authorization within 48 hours of deployment.
scenario_text: A regional police unit deployed a real-time facial recognition scan across three transit stations to locate a child reported missing from a nearby town. The deployment began at 9:14 p.m. and continued through the night while officers reviewed camera matches. The unit's legal liaison submitted the authorization request to the duty magistrate 36 hours after the scan began.

axis: exemption scope: research-use percentage required for the scientific-research exemption
rule_text: For an AI system developed exclusively for scientific research purposes to qualify for the research exemption, at least 90 percent of the system's intended use must be dedicated to research activity, and for an AI system developed for a mixed research-and-commercial deployment purpose to qualify for the research exemption, at least 50 percent of the system's intended use must be dedicated to research activity.
scenario_text: Marrow Institute built a protein-folding prediction tool intended solely to support its academic laboratory's publications and grant-funded studies. Before applying for the research exemption, the institute's technology transfer office logged how the tool's compute hours were allocated over the prior quarter. The audit found that 70 percent of the tool's usage hours were dedicated to research activity.

axis: exemption scope: regulatory sandbox user-count ceiling by pilot tier
rule_text: an AI system tested in a standard regulatory sandbox program retains its sandbox exemption from full conformity assessment as long as its cumulative user count stays below 1000 users, and an AI system tested in an extended regulatory sandbox program for large-scale pilots retains its sandbox exemption from full conformity assessment as long as its cumulative user count stays below 100 users.
scenario_text: Thessaly Health enrolled its symptom-triage chatbot in a standard regulatory sandbox program run by the national health authority. Over the pilot's first four months, the team tracked how many patients interacted with the chatbot through the sandbox portal. By the end of the reporting period, the chatbot had been used by 500 users.

rule_text: an AI system performing a narrow document-formatting procedural task remains eligible for the procedural-task exemption from high-risk classification while it affects fewer than 50 individuals per year, and an AI system performing a broader administrative case-triage task remains eligible for the procedural-task exemption from high-risk classification while it affects fewer than 5000 individuals per year.
scenario_text: Halvorsen Municipal Services uses an AI tool that reformats scanned permit applications into the standard digital template before routing them to a caseworker, with no substantive decision-making role. scenario_text: Amberglen Media developed an in-app banner module that displays promotional imagery between gameplay frames in a mobile game. The remediation project was completed 12 months after the applicability date.

axis: transition period: phase-out window for prohibited-practice deployments begun before vs after the prohibition's effective date
rule_text: An operator running a prohibited AI practice deployment that began after the prohibition's effective date must cease the practice within 12 months of the effective date, and an operator running a prohibited AI practice deployment that existed before the prohibition's effective date must cease the practice within 1 months of the effective date.
scenario_text: Harrowgate Insight launched a customer-profiling tool that combined behavioral and biometric signals into a single risk category, beginning operation shortly after the prohibition's effective date had already passed. Once the tool was flagged during an internal audit, the compliance team began winding down its use. The tool was fully decommissioned 6 months after the effective date.

axis: SAR filing deadline: alerts with an identified subject vs an unidentified subject
rule_text: A bank investigating an identified-subject suspicious activity alert must file a Suspicious Activity Report within 60 days of the initial detection, and a bank investigating an unidentified-subject suspicious activity alert must file a Suspicious Activity Report within 30 days of the initial detection.
scenario_text: Cobalt Trust Bank's monitoring system flagged a series of rapid transfers through a customer account, and investigators were able to confirm the identity of the account holder initiating the transfers on the first day of review. The bank's BSA officer submitted the Suspicious Activity Report 45 days after the alert was generated. The transfers totaled approximately $180,000 across eleven transactions.

axis: structuring alert escalation deadline: automated-system-flagged vs manually-referred alerts
rule_text: A compliance analyst reviewing an automated-system-flagged structuring alert must escalate the case to the BSA officer within 2 days of the alert, and a compliance analyst reviewing a manually-referred structuring alert must escalate the case to the BSA officer within 5 days of the alert.
scenario_text: Nimbus Pay's transaction monitoring engine automatically generated a structuring alert after a customer made four cash deposits of $2,800 each within a single week. The reviewing analyst, Priya Nadar, escalated the case file to the BSA officer 3 days after the alert appeared in the case queue. No further deposits were recorded during that window.

axis: crypto withdrawal hold period: newly-registered vs established accounts
rule_text: An exchange processing a withdrawal request from a newly-registered account must hold the funds for enhanced verification for 72 hours before release, and an exchange processing a withdrawal request from an established account must hold the funds for enhanced verification for 24 hours before release.
scenario_text: Brightline Exchange received a withdrawal request for 4.2 BTC from a customer whose account had been registered nine days earlier. The exchange's risk operations team released the funds 48 hours after the withdrawal request was submitted. The destination address had not previously appeared in the exchange's records.

axis: wire transfer recall window: domestic ACH vs international SWIFT transfers
rule_text: A bank processing a recall request for a domestic ACH transfer must complete the recall within 24 hours of the recall notice, and a bank processing a recall request for an international SWIFT transfer must complete the recall within 96 hours of the recall notice.
scenario_text: Anchorpoint Bank received a recall notice from a corporate customer after a domestic ACH payment of $42,000 was sent to an incorrect account number. The bank's operations team completed the recall 60 hours after receiving the notice. The receiving institution confirmed the funds had not yet been withdrawn.

Scenario: Solvex Bank launched a new credit-scoring system that uses automated profiling to set interest rates for loan applicants without human review. The project kickoff was recorded on June 1, and the impact assessment document was finalized and signed off 30 days later. The system evaluates applicants using an algorithmic model.

scenario_text: Falkirk Logistics detected irregular access logs on a server handling shipment data transferred between its offices in Germany and Poland. axis: purpose-limitation scope: statistical-research-compatible vs marketing-incompatible secondary purposes
rule_text: Under this purpose-compatibility framework, data originally collected for a stated purpose may be reused for a statistical-research-compatible secondary purposes if no more than 1 purposes are added without fresh consent, and data originally collected for a stated purpose may be reused for a marketing-incompatible secondary purposes if no more than 4 purposes are added without fresh consent.
scenario_text: Greymont Utilities collected household energy-usage data for billing purposes and later sought to reuse the dataset to support anonymized statistical research on regional consumption trends. The internal purpose log for this reuse request lists 2 purposes added to the original billing purpose. The added purposes relate to aggregate research analysis.

Scenario: Thistledown Bank operates a newly deployed cloud-based system for processing current account records, launched last year as part of its infrastructure modernization program. The system's audit-log retention schedule was configured to keep access trails for 4 years. The system is part of the bank's modernized transaction infrastructure.

axis: breach notification window: large-scale (500+ individuals) breach vs small-scale breach, individual notification deadline in days
rule_text: A covered entity experiencing a large-scale breach of unsecured protected health information must notify affected individuals within 60 days of discovery, and a covered entity experiencing a small-scale breach of unsecured protected health information must notify affected individuals within 30 days of discovery.
scenario_text: Rosewood Regional Medical Center discovered on March 3 that an unencrypted laptop containing patient billing records had been stolen from a locked office. The center's privacy officer determined the incident affected 1,150 patients across three clinics. The compliance team began mailing individual notification letters 45 days after the date of discovery.

axis: patient right-of-access response deadline: electronic portal-based records vs paper-based legacy records, in days
rule_text: A covered entity responding to an individual's request for access to electronic portal-based records must provide the requested records within 30 days of receiving the request, and a covered entity responding to an individual's request for access to paper-based records must provide the requested records within 45 days of receiving the request.
scenario_text: Harbor View Medical Group received a written request from a patient asking for a full copy of her records, which are maintained entirely within the practice's certified electronic health record system. The health information management department logged the request on June 2 and began compiling the electronic file. Staff completed and delivered the records to the patient 37 days after the request was logged.

axis: security risk analysis review cycle: high-risk information system vs low-risk information system, review interval in months
rule_text: A covered entity operating a high-risk information system must conduct a documented security risk analysis review at least every 12 months, and a covered entity operating a low-risk information system must conduct a documented security risk analysis review at least every 24 months.
scenario_text: Cedarbrook Health Network classified its patient portal server, which stores payment card data alongside PHI and accepts external logins, as a system carrying elevated exposure to unauthorized access. The IT security team scheduled its documented risk analysis reviews for this server at intervals of 18 months.

axis: audit log retention period: systems storing psychotherapy notes vs systems storing general clinical records, in years
rule_text: A covered entity maintaining audit logs for systems that store psychotherapy notes must retain those audit logs for at least 6 years, and a covered entity maintaining audit logs for systems that store general clinical records must retain those audit logs for at least 10 years.
scenario_text: Lakeside Behavioral Health Associates operates a dedicated software module in which its therapists record session notes documenting the content of patient counseling conversations, separate from the shared clinical chart. The organization's IT policy set the audit log retention period for this module's server at 8 years.

axis: de-identification safe harbor: number of identifier categories removed under the Safe Harbor method vs the Limited Data Set method
rule_text: A covered entity de-identifying a dataset under the Safe Harbor method must remove at least 14 identifier categories of direct and indirect patient identifiers, and a covered entity de-identifying a dataset under the Limited Data Set method must remove at least 18 identifier categories of direct and indirect patient identifiers.
scenario_text: Meridian Health Analytics prepared a research dataset intended for public release with no data use agreement restricting the recipient, drawing from five years of oncology visit records. The data governance team stripped identifier fields from the export and logged that the final file had 16 identifier categories removed before the dataset was released.

axis: incidental disclosure exception: minimum physical separation distance in a high-volume walk-in setting vs a scheduled appointment-based setting, in feet
rule_text: A covered entity operating a high-volume walk-in care setting must maintain at least 3 feet of separation between patient check-in conversation areas and the public waiting area to rely on the incidental disclosure exception, and a covered entity operating a scheduled appointment-based care setting must maintain at least 6 feet of separation between patient check-in conversation areas and the public waiting area to rely on the incidental disclosure exception.
scenario_text: Sunview Urgent Care redesigned its front desk after noticing that unscheduled patients frequently queued within earshot of the intake counter during peak afternoon hours. The facilities team measured the renovated layout and confirmed that the check-in counter sits 4.5 feet from the nearest waiting area seating.

axis: IRB continuing review interval for authorization waiver: expedited-review research protocol vs full-board-review research protocol, in months
rule_text: An institutional review board overseeing an expedited-review research protocol that waives individual authorization for use of protected health information must conduct continuing review at least every 6 months, and an institutional review board overseeing a full-board-review research protocol that waives individual authorization for use of protected health information must conduct continuing review at least every 12 months.
scenario_text: Dr. Amara Osei's retrospective chart-review study of diabetes medication adherence was classified by the university IRB as posing no more than minimal risk to subjects and involving only existing records. The IRB approved a waiver of authorization for the study and scheduled its continuing review at intervals of 9 months.

axis: GINA remediation deadline: pre-GINA legacy health plan enrollment vs post-GINA new enrollment, in months
rule_text: A health plan administering benefits under a pre-GINA legacy enrollment must complete remediation of any underwriting documents that used genetic information within 6 months of identifying the issue, and a health plan administering benefits under a post-GINA new enrollment must complete remediation of any underwriting documents that used genetic information within 18 months of identifying the issue.
scenario_text: Statewide Employer Health Plan discovered during an internal audit that an enrollee's 2008 underwriting file, opened before the plan updated its intake forms for GINA, contained a family medical history questionnaire referencing hereditary cancer risk. The compliance team began remediating the file and completed the correction 10 months after the issue was identified.

axis: public health emergency waiver duration: facility inside declared disaster area vs affiliated facility outside declared disaster area, in hours
rule_text: During a declared public health emergency, a facility located within the declared disaster area may rely on the Secretary's waiver of sanctions for specified HIPAA requirements for up to 24 hours after the disaster declaration, and during a declared public health emergency, an affiliated facility located outside the declared disaster area may rely on the Secretary's waiver of sanctions for specified HIPAA requirements for up to 72 hours after the disaster declaration.
scenario_text: Following a declared public health emergency after a hurricane made landfall, Coastal Memorial Hospital, situated directly within the officially designated disaster area, began operating under emergency protocols including relaxed procedures for obtaining patient acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices. The hospital's emergency operations log shows these relaxed procedures remained in effect for 48 hours after the disaster declaration was issued.
